item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption provides guidance on recognising, disclosing and managing conflicts of interest in public agencies.
item.support: It explains how to identify, disclose and manage a conflict of interest

item.text: Its framework examines personal interests, public duties and whether an informed observer could perceive that private interests might be favoured.
item.support: Could a reasonable person perceive that the personal interest might be favoured?
item.section: What is a conflict of interest?

item.text: The Commission explains that a conflict usually does not itself amount to corruption, but concealment, misuse or poor management can lead to corrupt conduct.
item.support: Corrupt conduct can, however, arise when a conflict of interest is concealed, understated, mismanaged or abused.
item.section: Conflicts of interest and corrupt conduct

item.text: The Commission advises managers to assess risks, document and implement responses, monitor changes and audit whether controls work.
item.support: The relevant manager should review the written declaration of a conflict of interest and prepare a plan for managing and monitoring it.
item.section: Manage and monitor conflicts of interest

item.quote: As with any other important control framework, an agency’s conflict of interest framework should be evaluated or audited from time-to-time.
